extracted.name: Standard Visitor visa
extracted.description: The Standard Visitor visa allows you to visit the UK for tourism, business, study (up to 6 months), and other permitted activities. You can usually stay for up to 6 months.
eligibilityCriteria: You must have a passport or travel document to enter the UK. It should be valid for the whole of your stay.
You must be able to show that you'll leave the UK at the end of your visit
You must be able to show that you're able to support yourself and your dependants during your trip (or have funding from someone else to support you)
You must be able to show that you're able to pay for your return or onward journey (or have funding from someone else to pay for the journey)
You must be able to show that you'll not live in the UK for extended periods through frequent or successive visits, or make the UK your main home
requiredDocuments: the dates you’re planning to travel to the UK
where you’ll be staying during your visit
how much you think your trip will cost
your current home address and how long you’ve lived there
your parents’ names and dates of birth (if known)
how much you earn in a year (if you have an income)
details of any criminal, civil or immigration offences you may have committed
details of your travel history for the past 10 years
your employer’s address and telephone number
your partner’s name, date of birth and passport number
the name and address of anyone paying for your trip
the name, address and passport number of any family members you have in the UK
a certificate proving that you’ve had a tuberculosis (TB) test if you’re visiting for more than 6 months

extracted.name: Student visa
extracted.description: The Student visa allows individuals aged 16 or over to study in the UK at a licensed student sponsor. Applicants must have an unconditional offer, sufficient funds, and English language proficiency. The visa permits work under certain conditions and can be extended or switched to other routes.

You've been offered a place on a course by a licensed student sponsor
You have enough money to support yourself and pay for your course
You can speak, read, write and understand English
You have consent from your parents if you're 16 or 17

extracted.name: Graduate visa
extracted.description: A Graduate visa allows you to stay in the UK for at least 18 months after successfully completing an eligible course with a Student visa. The duration is 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, or 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027; PhD graduates get 3 years.
eligibilityCriteria: you’re in the UK
your current visa is a Student visa or Tier 4 (General) student visa
you studied a UK bachelor’s degree, postgraduate degree or other eligible course for a minimum period of time with your Student visa or Tier 4 (General) student visa
your education provider (such as your university or college) has told the Home Office you’ve successfully completed your course
requiredDocuments: a valid passport or other travel document that shows your identity and nationality
your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) reference number from when you applied for your Student visa or Tier 4 (General) student visa
your biometric residence permit (BRP)
proof of your relationship with your partner or children if they’re applying with you
a letter from your scholarship or sponsorship provider approving your application, if they paid for both your course fees and living costs in the last 12 months
a certified translation

extracted.name: Family visa
extracted.description: A visa to live with a family member in the UK for more than 6 months. You can apply as a partner, child, parent, or relative providing long-term care.

feeComponents.label: Application fee (joining partner, parent or child)

eligibilityCriteria: You and your partner both need to be 18 or over (if applying as a partner).
Your partner must be a British or Irish citizen, have settled status, pre-settled status, a Turkish Businessperson or Worker visa, protection status, or permission to stay as a stateless person.
You and your partner must intend to live together permanently in the UK.
You must prove your relationship (e.g., marriage, civil partnership, or living together for at least 2 years).
You must prove you have a good knowledge of English.
You must meet the financial requirements (minimum income requirement of £29,000 per year, unless exempt).

your date of birth

your tuberculosis test results if you’re from a country where you have to take the test
a certified translation of any document that is not in English or Welsh
online proof of your immigration status if you have an eVisa - you’ll need to get a share code
your biometric residence permit (BRP) - you can use it for 24 months after the expiry date printed on your card or until 31 December 2026, whichever comes first

extracted.name: Global Talent visa
extracted.description: A visa for leaders or potential leaders in academia or research, arts and culture, or digital technology to work in the UK. Applicants must be at least 18 years old and either have won an eligible prestigious prize or obtained an endorsement from a Home Office approved organisation.
eligibilityCriteria: You must be a leader or potential leader in academia or research, arts and culture, or digital technology.
You must be at least 18 years old.
If you have not won an eligible prestigious prize, you must obtain an endorsement from a Home Office approved organisation.
If applying based on an endorsement, you must apply within 3 months of receiving your endorsement letter.
The endorsing organisation must not have withdrawn its approval.

endorsement or an eligible prestigious prize
field: academia/research, arts and culture or digital technology
actual: You must be a leader or potential leader in academia or research, arts and culture, or digital technology.
You must be at least 18 years old.
If you have not won an eligible prestigious prize, you must obtain an endorsement from a Home Office approved organisation.
If applying based on an endorsement, you must apply within 3 months of receiving your endorsement letter.
The endorsing organisation must not have withdrawn its approval.
